name: Jehoiachin
bio:
Jehoiachin succeeded his father Jehoiakim as king of Judah at eighteen, reigning only three months in Jerusalem; his mother was Nehushta, daughter of Elnathan. He did evil in the LORD's eyes like his father. Nebuchadnezzar's forces besieged Jerusalem, and Jehoiachin surrendered himself, his mother, his officials, and his princes to the king of Babylon in Nebuchadnezzar's eighth year. Nebuchadnezzar stripped the temple and palace treasures, destroyed Solomon's gold vessels, and deported Jehoiachin along with the royal family, officials, craftsmen, and thousands of leading citizens to Babylon, installing his uncle Mattaniah (renamed Zedekiah) as king in his place (2 Kings 24:8-17).

## 📖 Core Story: Released from Prison

After thirty-seven years in captivity, Jehoiachin was released from prison by Evil-Merodach, king of Babylon, in the first year of his reign. Evil-Merodach spoke kindly to him, gave him a seat of honor above the other captive kings in Babylon, provided new clothes in place of his prison garments, and granted him a regular daily allowance for the rest of his life (2 Kings 25:27-30). Chronicles gives his age as eight rather than eighteen and specifies the length of his reign as three months and ten days (2 Chronicles 36:9).
